worldcombat.skill.bloodmoon.summary: Call a full moon that shines red as blood in front of the user, then pour the whole spirit into a thick, straight moonlight beam: it strikes the nearest foe first and pierces a limited line of foes behind, stopping at any block. Once spent, it cannot be called again for a while; using another move lets the spirit settle early. Eclipse style widens the beam and pierces more of the line, at some cost to the primary hit.
worldcombat.skill.bloodmoon.use.0: Call a full moon and fire a thick moonlight beam
worldcombat.skill.bloodmoon.use.1: Pierce a whole line of foes at once
worldcombat.skill.bloodmoon.use.2: Pick off a far, bulky target
The beam deals about %1$s special damage to the nearest foe; other non-allies further along the same line each take about %2$s special damage. Beam length %3$s blocks, cut short by blocks.
The beam is %1$s blocks half-width and pierces at most %2$s foes behind the first.
Afterwards it cannot be called again for %1$s; using any other move lets the spirit settle early.
worldcombat.skill.bloodmoon.eclipse.on: Eclipse style now: the beam is thicker and pierces more of the line, with a shorter charge; the primary hit is x0.85.
worldcombat.skill.bloodmoon.eclipse.off: Full moon style now: a thinner beam that hits the first foe and only a few behind, full power on the primary, longer charge.
worldcombat.skill.bloodmoon.timing: Range %1$s blocks, windup %2$s, recovery %3$s, costs %4$s PP, cooldown %5$s.
worldcombat.skill.bloodmoon.growth.0: From level %1$s the primary rises to %2$s and the lined splash to %3$s.
worldcombat.skill.bloodmoon.growth.1: From level %1$s the primary is %2$s, the lined splash %3$s and the beam half-width %4$s blocks.
worldcombat.skill.bloodmoon.preference.e: On: the beam is thicker and pierces more of the line, with a shorter charge; the primary hit is x0.85. Off (full moon): a thinner beam that hits the first foe and only a few behind, full power on the primary, longer charge.
worldcombat.skill.bloodmoon.preference.a: Beyond this distance it will not call the moon and closes in first.
Below this health fraction it will not call the moon unless the target is nearly down. Higher values make it more protective and less likely to finish a weakened foe.
On (with eclipse style): it calls the moon more readily when other enemies stand in line behind the target, since the beam can pierce the whole row; off ranks by the single-target payoff only.
